questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L03_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.4

A number cube is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a 1 or a 2?

feedback.text: Correct. The outcomes 1 and 2 are two favorable outcomes out of six total.
This counts only one outcome. The word or includes both 1 and 2.
This incorrectly multiplies. An or question uses addition or counting the union.
This counts too many outcomes. Only 1 and 2 are favorable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L03_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.4

A number cube is rolled. What is the probability of rolling an even number or a number greater than 4?

feedback.text: This counts 6 twice. The overlap must be subtracted or listed once.
Correct. The union is {2, 4, 5, 6}, which is 4 outcomes out of 6.
This is only the overlap, not the full union.
This counts only the even outcomes and leaves out 5.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L03_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.5

A coin is flipped and a number cube is rolled. What is the probability of heads and rolling a 6?

feedback.text: This adds counts from two different sample spaces. Independent and means multiply probabilities.
This only uses the number cube event and ignores the coin.
Correct. Multiply 1/2 by 1/6 to get 1/12.
This adds probabilities instead of multiplying for both events happening.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L03_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.5

Two fair coins are flipped. What is the probability of getting heads on both coins?

feedback.text: This is the probability for one coin only. Two coins require both events.
This assumes both outcomes must happen, but probability must compare favorable outcomes to all outcomes.
This counts outcomes with at least one head, not both heads.
Correct. The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT, and only HH has heads on both coins.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MCR_U05_L03_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.MCR.PR.4

A number cube is rolled. What is the probability of rolling an odd number or a 6?

feedback.text: This counts only odd outcomes and leaves out 6.
Correct. The favorable outcomes are {1, 3, 5, 6}, or 4 out of 6.
This counts only rolling a 6.
This incorrectly multiplies for an or question.
